newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms on liquidity concerns.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms on liquidity concerns.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in active late trading on Tuesday on concerns over money market conditions, dealers said.
They said the money market was fluctuating throughout the day, keeping the dollar-rupiah rate volatile.
One U.S. bank dealer said the dollar rebounded briefly at midday as liquidity was ample, but fell in the afternoon on rises in the overnight rate.
Spot rupiah was last at 2,397.25/97.75 at 0930 GMT after having fallen to the 2,340 level from a high of 2,397.0. It opened at 2,401.0/02.0 on Tuesday.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,396.75/97.50 and 2,398.50/99.25, respectively. Tom/next was at 0.45/0.60.
Overnight money rose to 21.0 percent after easing to 12.0/12.5 percent at midday. Dealers said higher tax payments at the end of the 1996/97 fiscal year were the main cause.
"The market is mainly liquidity-driven," one said.
Another dealer said some players wanted to link the dollar selling to a possible band widening by the central bank but they seemed to have failed to drive the market to follow.
"Liquidity is the main issue. We have only two more days to settle all the outstanding taxes," the dealer said.
The market will be closed on Friday for a public holiday and Monday for the fiscal year-end and reopen on April 1.
"Operators are bullish on the rupiah at present. But they are alert if market sentiment turns around when liquidity conditions change," the U.S. bank dealer said.
Swap rates continued to edge up as the rupiah remained well bid in the wake of the fiscal year-end.
One-month swaps rose to 12.0/12.5 from 10.5/11.5, two to 24.0/25.0 from 22.5/24.0, three to 35.0/36.0 from 34.0/35.0 and six to 70.5/72.0 from 69.0/70.0 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point on Tuesday to 2,392/2,584 and the conversion band to 2,392/2,440.
One foreign bank dealer said earlier a possible rate hike in the United States had only marginal impact on the market.
"The focus is on liquidity. A possible hike seems to have been widely discounted," the dealer said.
"Besides, this is positive in the sense that it would narrow interest rate differentials between the two currencies and help curb recent heavy capital inflows," he added.
